newsitem.title: USA: Morris said to deny comment on Hillary files role.
newsitem.headline: Morris said to deny comment on Hillary files role.

text.p: Disgraced former Clinton political strategist Dick Morris has denied telling a prostitute Hillary Rodham Clinton ordered a controversial review of FBI files and has promised to give a committee of Congress a sworn statement on Monday, officials said.

Morris, who resigned two weeks ago after the supermarket tabloid Star reported he had an affair with the prostitute, promised to give Representative William Clinger's House of Representatives Government Reform Committee a sworn statement by the end of the day on whether the first lady ordered the review, the committee said.

But the committee for the re-election of President Bill Clinton and Al Gore said Morris had already denied the prostitute's claim that he made such a comment. "Mr. Morris called Peter Knight, the campaign manager, and specifically denied that he ever told anyone that Mrs. Clinton was involved in the FBI files," campaign spokesman Joe Lockhart said.

Sherry Rowlands, a prostitute who claimed a year-long affair with Morris, said in a diary excerpt published by the Star that she asked Morris who ordered the FBI files review. "He said, 'It was Hillary in 1993. She ordered them. She's a paranoid lady -- she did it,'" the diary said.

Several Republican congressmen have accused the Clinton White House of reviewing up to 900 FBI files to look for political dirt on Republicans but President Bill Clinton has said the review appeared to be an honest mistake.

Former Clinton aides acknowledged they ordered the FBI to send them the background files on former White House officials but said it was because they mistakenly believed the former aides still had White House passes. The files they ordered included those of former Secretary of State James Baker and former White House spokesman Marlin Fitzwater.

Clinger, a Pennsylvania Republican, said in a letter to Morris that he expected his sworn statement on the prostitute's claim by 5 p.m. because Morris promised committee investigators he would deliver it by then.

"We request that you affirm by sworn statement the truthfulness of comments attributed to you by Ms. Rowlands," the letter said. "We ask that you include in such a statement any additional information known to you regarding the FBI files matter."
Clinger also asked Morris for all correspondence, E-mail and any other records he has on the subject.
